speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with postmenopausal bleeding and an adnexal mass; to understand the underlying cause, I will need to ask you a series of questions. First, how old were you when you last had a menstrual period, and how long has this bleeding been occurring?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old woman. The patient presents with a 2-month history of intermittent postmenopausal bleeding. She denies any recent weight loss, fever, or changes in bladder or bowel habits. No previous history of similar symptoms. She has no history of serious illness and takes no medications regularly.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since you are a 65-year-old with a 2-month history of postmenopausal bleeding and an adnexal mass, I need to determine if this is related to the ovary or the uterus. Are you currently taking any hormone replacement therapy or herbal supplements?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Intermittent bleeding from the vagina. I also have No recent weight loss, No fever, No changes in bladder or bowel habits.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Endometrial hyperplasia with concurrent benign ovarian cyst (simple cyst)
The absence of weight loss, fever, or bowel changes makes malignancy less likely, but the combination of postmenopausal bleeding and an adnexal mass requires imaging to rule out ovarian cancer. REQUEST IMAGES: Transvaginal ultrasound of pelvis.
